items.title: Defend against dummy’s long suit
items.text:
In notrump, a long suit in dummy can produce several tricks if declarer has a way to reach it. On this hand, you’ll pause after winning the ♥K and decide what to lead next.

Open annotated BBO HandViewer (new tab)

Use Next to step through the replay and pause at the coaching prompts.

Board 15 · Defensive play

West is declarer in 3NT after 1♠ – 2♥ – 3NT with the opponents passing throughout. You are North.

Visible hand ♠ ♥ ♦ ♣ North AQ K93 Q843 J732 East (dummy) J84 QJT852 J962 —

You led the ♦3. Dummy played the jack, South won the king and West followed with the seven. South returned the ♣10 and West won the queen. West led the ♥6, and your king won as dummy played the two and South the four.

Pause here. Count dummy’s remaining hearts. What could a heart return do for declarer? Compare it with a diamond switch.

Reveal the defence and declarer’s entry

Consider a diamond switch. Your ♥K just removed the main obstacle to dummy’s hearts. South’s ♦K on trick one and your remaining ♦Q give you a reason to explore diamonds. A switch makes declarer arrange the heart entry independently.

Recorded play. North returned the ♥3. West won the ♥A and used the ♥7 to reach dummy. Dummy won four heart tricks. West made 3NT exactly.

From declarer’s seat. With ♥A76 opposite ♥QJT852, West used the six to drive out the king and retained the seven as a route to dummy.

Result check. The packet has no traveller for Board 15. The recorded line illustrates the entry. A switch is an alternative to investigate.

Check your understanding

Count dummy’s winners and ask how declarer will reach them. Before returning dummy’s suit, check whether your lead helps create or preserve that entry.

items.title: Describe opener’s long suit
items.text:
Opener’s second bid helps responder picture the hand. Here you’ll choose between repeating a six-card club suit, bidding diamonds, and rebidding notrump. Think about what partner would expect from each call.

Open annotated BBO HandViewer (new tab)

Use Next to step through the replay and pause at the coaching prompts.

Board 2 · Standard SAYC

East passed. South opened 1♣ (Introduce), West passed, North responded 1♠ (Explore), and East passed. You are South. North–South are vulnerable.

♠ A · ♥ K4 · ♦ KQ98 · ♣ K98753

Choose your rebid (Clarify). Compare 1NT, 2♣ and 2♦. What shape and strength will partner infer?

Reveal the bidding discussion

I favour 2♣. You have six clubs and a singleton spade. Repeating clubs naturally puts the long suit on the table. A 1NT rebid suggests a more balanced hand, and 2♦ is a reverse that asks partner to go to 3♣ to return to your first suit. With 15 HCP and modest club texture, I prefer the simple rebid to a stronger action. ACBL SAYC booklet

Decide. After a hypothetical 2♣ rebid, North can reassess 11 HCP and four clubs opposite the announced length. Discuss how to invite further bidding and what would make you choose clubs or notrump.

Reveal the recorded result and traveller

South rebid 1NT and North returned to 2♣. South took eleven tricks. Four tables made 3NT and three made 5♣. Those results show what happened on this deal.

Check your understanding

Why does 2♦ put more pressure on responder than 2♣? To prefer clubs after 2♦, responder has to bid at the three level.

items.title: How should a passed hand invite in spades?
items.text:
A limit raise asks opener to decide whether the partnership has enough for game. You’ll make that decision from both seats, starting with what a passed hand can show when partner opens 1♠.

Open annotated BBO HandViewer (new tab)

Use Next to step through the replay and pause at the coaching prompts.

Improving club players · 15 minutes · Standard SAYC
path: How should a passed hand invite in spades?

items.title: Board 4 · Your call as North
items.text:
West deals. Both sides are vulnerable.

West Pass → North Pass → East Pass → South 1♠ (Introduce) → West Pass → North ? (Explore)

♠ AQ9 · ♥ 84 · ♦ 853 · ♣ AJ972

Choose a call. How many trumps do you have, and do you want to sign off, invite, or commit to game?

Reveal the bidding discussion and recorded result

Bid 3♠, a natural limit raise. You have 11 HCP, three spades headed by A–Q, and a side ace. Treat the hand as invitational. The small doubleton can help, but the flat 5–3–3–2 shape and lack of red-suit honours give little reason to upgrade. In standard SAYC, the direct limit raise can be made with three or more trumps. A direct 2♣ is a natural club bid. ACBL SAYC System Booklet

Rule of thumb. With three or more trumps and roughly 10–11 dummy points, raise a one-major opening directly to three of the major to invite game. The earlier pass helps opener judge your upper limit.

Common exception. With only two trumps, use a natural response appropriate to your hand. The limit raise promises at least three.

Recorded auction. North raised to 3♠ (Explore), and South bid 4♠ (Clarify). The pair’s actual agreement for 3♠ is unconfirmed. Reading it as a SAYC limit raise, South should pass with 11 HCP, five spades headed by the jack, and no singleton or void. The fourth-seat opening is already light in high cards, and the four-card heart suit gives little reason to accept on its own.

Traveller. South played 4♠ down three. It was the only spade game among 16 tables. Five tables stopped in 3♠ and all went down. Two played 2♠ and one made it. Those results show how this deal played across the field. North’s invitation and South’s acceptance are two decisions to assess separately.
path: How should a passed hand invite in spades?

items.title: Variation · One more trump
items.text:
Same auction and vulnerability. Replace the ♥4 with the ♠4.

♠ AQ94 · ♥ 8 · ♦ 853 · ♣ AJ972

What does the fourth spade change? Would you still invite?

Reveal the variation

3♠ is still a reasonable invitation. The extra trump and singleton heart make this hand stronger in support. A fourth-seat opener can be light, so there is still value in letting South decide whether to bid game.
path: How should a passed hand invite in spades?

items.title: Fresh hand · Make your call as opener
items.text:
Both sides are vulnerable. After three passes, you open 1♠ as South (Introduce). West passes, North raises to 3♠ (Explore), and East passes.

♠ KJ974 · ♥ AQ73 · ♦ 84 · ♣ J6

What do you call (Clarify)? What extra playing strength, if any, do you have opposite the limit raise?

Reveal the fresh hand

Pass. You have 11 HCP, five trumps and no singleton or void. The four-card heart suit offers some potential, but the hand is a minimum for your fourth-seat opening.
path: How should a passed hand invite in spades?

items.title: Independent check
items.text:
You passed initially. Partner opens 1♠ in fourth seat and the next player passes. You have invitational values and exactly three spades. What do you bid in standard SAYC?

Check your answer

3♠. It is a natural limit raise, and three trumps are enough. Opener can pass with a minimum.

Alternative Conventions

One-way Reverse Drury: After a third- or fourth-seat major opening, a passed hand can use artificial 2♣ to show a good raise with at least three trumps. Opener can stop in 2♠ with a minimum.

Two-way Drury: One common agreement uses 2♣ for a good raise with exactly three trumps and 2♦ for a good raise with four or more. Pairs playing Drury should also agree on the meaning of a direct 3♠. Larry Cohen’s Drury notes
path: How should a passed hand invite in spades?

items.title: When should I raise partner’s overcall?
items.text:
When partner overcalls, even a modest hand may be worth a raise. You’ll decide whether three hearts and useful side honours are enough to support partner after a 2♥ overcall.

Open annotated BBO HandViewer (new tab)

Use Next to step through the replay and pause at the coaching prompts.

Improving club players · 15 minutes · Standard SAYC
path: When should I raise partner’s overcall?

items.title: Board 3 · Your call as East
items.text:
South deals. East–West vulnerable.

South 1♠ (Introduce) → West 2♥ (overcall) → North Pass → East ?

♠ A9863 · ♥ JT3 · ♦ K73 · ♣ 65

Choose Pass, 3♥, or 2♠. Which of your cards are likely to help West take tricks? Are you willing to play 3♥ if West has a minimum?

Reveal the bidding discussion and recorded result

I favour 3♥, a natural, nonforcing raise. You have 8 HCP, three trumps headed by J–10, a side ace and a doubleton club. The ♦K may help, depending on West’s shape and where the ♦A lies. That is enough to consider raising a sound two-level overcall. Pass is defensible at adverse vulnerability if you judge the hand too marginal to risk the three level.

Rule of thumb. With three trumps opposite a sound two-level overcall, count useful trump honours and likely side winners. Raise when you are willing to play at the next level opposite a minimum. With stronger game interest, 2♠ is the SAYC cue-bid that forces a reply and asks about the quality of the overcall. East’s hand is light for that call. The booklet specifies the cue-bid treatment and leaves the exact strength of this simple 3♥ raise unstated. ACBL SAYC System Booklet

Common exception. When the support is poor and the side honours are unlikely to take tricks, passing can be right with three trumps. Vulnerability makes a marginal three-level raise less attractive.

Recorded result. East passed. West played 2♥ and took 11 tricks. West held 17 HCP, seven hearts headed by A–K–Q, and a diamond void. The partnership had ten trumps, and East’s ♦K faced a void.

Traveller. Eight of 16 tables bid and made 4♥. Six took eleven tricks and two took twelve. Those results describe this deal. At the decision, East had the auction, the eight high-card points and the SAYC meanings of the available calls to go on.
path: When should I raise partner’s overcall?

items.title: Variation · One more trump
items.text:
Same auction and vulnerability. Replace the ♠3 with the ♥4.

♠ A986 · ♥ JT43 · ♦ K73 · ♣ 65

Does the fourth heart change your call or your confidence in it?

Reveal the variation

Bid 3♥. The fourth trump makes the natural raise more attractive at the same 8 HCP. You have better support even if West has only five hearts.
path: When should I raise partner’s overcall?

items.title: Fresh hand
items.text:
Same auction and vulnerability.

♠ 74 · ♥ Q84 · ♦ A865 · ♣ KQ62

Which call asks West to describe the quality of the overcall? Which cards give you game interest?

Reveal the fresh hand

Bid 2♠. The trump queen, side ace and ♣KQ give you 11 HCP and useful support. The forcing cue-bid lets West return to 3♥ with a minimum. You can pass that rebid.
path: When should I raise partner’s overcall?

items.title: Independent check
items.text:
After (1♠)–2♥–(Pass), what is the difference between 3♥ and 2♠ in SAYC?

Check your answer

3♥ is a natural, nonforcing heart raise. 2♠ cues the opener’s suit, forces a reply and asks about the quality of partner’s overcall.

Alternative Conventions

Some pairs agree that direct 3♥ after this exact auction is invitational. Others use a weak raise, often requiring four trumps, and reserve 2♠ for an invitational-or-better raise with support. Agree on both strength and trump length. Larry Cohen’s example of an invitational 3♥
path: When should I raise partner’s overcall?

items.title: Open a strong hand with a seven-card major
items.text:
A seven-card suit gives you two very different ways to start the auction. You’ll compare a one-level opening with a preempt and consider what each tells partner about your strength outside the long suit.

Open annotated BBO HandViewer (new tab)

Use Next to step through the replay and pause at the coaching prompts.

Board 10 · Standard SAYC

East deals and both sides are vulnerable. You are East, first to act.

♠ AK · ♥ KJT8743 · ♦ JT · ♣ A8

Choose your opening bid (Introduce). What would partner infer from 1♥ or 3♥?

Reveal the bidding discussion

Open 1♥. With 16 HCP, seven hearts and two outside aces, you want room for partner to describe their hand. A preemptive 3♥ opening invites partner to judge game facing a much weaker hand. After 1♥, use the next round to show your extra playing strength in light of partner’s response.

Explore. West actually held three hearts headed by the queen and the ♣K. Ask what West could communicate after 1♥, then consider East’s next call. Treat this as a bidding exercise with an open continuation.

Reveal the recorded result and traveller

East opened 3♥ and played there, taking ten tricks. Nine tables bid and made 4♥ exactly.

Check your understanding

Before opening a long major at the three level, name the outside winners partner would miss if they interpreted the opening as a preempt. Here they include the ♠A, ♠K and ♣A.
path: Open a strong hand with a seven-card major

items.title: November 2 with Bea and Bruno
items.text:
16 recorded deals and 10 travellers.

Start with Boards 3 and 4. Compare a raise after an overcall with a passed-hand limit raise, then decide whether the partner who hears the raise should bid game.

items.title: Board 3 — Show support after partner overcalls
items.text: Bea passed over Bruno’s 2♥ with three hearts, the ♠A, the ♦K and 8 HCP. Bruno took eleven tricks in 2♥. Eight of sixteen tables bid and made 4♥. Compare pass with a natural 3♥ raise under standard SAYC, then replay Bruno’s decision if he hears that raise.

items.title: Board 4 — Decide whether to accept a limit raise
items.text: Georgena’s passed-hand 3♠ invites game in standard SAYC. Bob had 11 HCP, five spades headed by the jack and two cards in each minor. Pass 3♠ with that minimum. The recorded 4♠ went down three. All six tables in 3♠ or 4♠ went down.

items.title: Board 2 — Describe opener’s long suit
items.text: After 1♣ – 1♠, Bob rebid 1NT with 15 HCP, a singleton spade and six clubs. Compare 2♣ with 1NT and discuss what each tells Georgena. Four tables made 3NT and three made 5♣. The recorded 2♣ took eleven tricks.

items.title: Board 10 — Leave room to show a strong seven-card major
items.text: Bea opened 3♥ with 16 HCP, seven hearts, the ♠AK and the ♣A. With a standard preemptive 3♥ agreement, prefer 1♥ and leave room for Bruno to show support. Nine tables made 4♥ exactly.

items.title: Board 15 — Count dummy’s winners and entries
items.text: Pause after Georgena wins the ♥K in 3NT. Compare a heart return with a switch. From Bruno’s seat, identify the heart entry to Bea’s long suit. The recorded heart return gave Bruno time to reach dummy. The traveller for this board was unavailable in the packet.
